(a) Documentation Required.—The Secretary of the Air Force shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the B–52 commercial engine replacement program of the Air Force. 
    (b) Contents.—The report submitted under subsection (a) shall include the following:
        (1) The acquisition strategy of the Secretary for the program. 
        (2) The cost and schedule estimates of the Secretary for the program. 
        (3) The key performance parameters or equivalent requirements document for the program. 
        (4) The test and evaluation strategy of the Secretary for the program. 
        (5) The logistics strategy of the Secretary for the program. 
        (6) The post-production fielding strategy of the Secretary for the program. 
        (7) An assessment of the potential for the commercial engine replacement to achieve nuclear system certification.  
    (c) Limitation.—Of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2020 for the Air Force, not more than 75 percent may be obligated or expended until the date on which the Secretary of the Air Force 
submits to the congressional defense committees the report required by subsection (a).

fable.w: The section only requires the Secretary of the Air Force to report to the congressional defense committees and conditions funding on that report. Congress is inside the federal government, so a report to its committees is not participation by outside parties. The word "commercial" in the program name might suggest industry involvement, but no contractor, expert, state, or member of the public is consulted or given any role in a federal decision.
fable.s: The Secretary of the Air Force shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the B–52 commercial engine replacement program of the Air Force.

opus.w: The only process here is a report from the Secretary of the Air Force to the congressional defense committees, plus a limit on spending funds until that report is submitted. It might look like participation because a funding decision depends on the report. But the Secretary and the congressional committees are both inside the federal government. No state, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted or brought into the decision.
opus.s: The Secretary of the Air Force shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the B–52 commercial engine replacement program of the Air Force.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of the Air Force to submit a report to congressional defense committees. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are not participation because they do not involve parties outside the federal government. There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of the Air Force shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the B–52 commercial engine replacement program of the Air Force.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report is required before funds can be obligated, it constitutes a procedural step involving outside parties. However, the recipient of the report is the "congressional defense committees." Congress is part of the federal government (inside the boundary). Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside entities.
